declared.title: One Size Does Not Make All Happy: Idionomic Links Between Striving for Positive States and Happiness in Experience Sampling
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex: works citing Mauss 2011, published 2023 to 2026 (2026-11-22); reports/chasing-happiness/counter-evidence.md (card 10)

population: 167 students of a public university in the western US, 76% women, 3 prompts a day for a week (2,251 surveys; full text)

findings.text: Moments of worry about one's happiness (« I worried about my positive emotions fading »: the EA items, full text) were followed by less happiness in the same person

support.sentence: Multilevel vector autoregressive models showed that EA consistently dampened happiness within-person, despite no between-person association.

findings.text: Doing one's best to stay happy went with more happiness for one group; for the other it did nothing directly and lowered happiness only through worry

support.sentence: In contrast, PP was linked to higher happiness in one group, but in the other, it had no direct benefit and indirectly reduced happiness via its connection to EA.

limits: one week, students of one US university
« experiential attachment » is measured by worry items: it is the worry, not another form of wanting (full text)
the two groups are found by the analysis, not set in advance; nothing manipulated
allegiance: co-authors (Hayes, Levin, Krafft) develop acceptance and commitment therapy, where « experiential attachment » comes from
